C-TEST-TIME-BUDGET-3-7950A760.Summary: T3 change on `RM-GOVERNED-PATH`: **the test-time budget.** The maintainer's target is an order-of-magnitude reduction in development wall time, measured before it is pinned. Act 1 measured the population — 2017 tests across 64 files in 138.83 s; 22 tests ≥ 1.0 s carrying 52.6 % of the suite; `validate:ci` executing **2424 test runs for 2017 distinct tests** (407 duplicates, 49.38 s) with the `validate` job running `validate:determinism` a third time; and the dominant cost being **O(n²) re-derivation of the immutable archive**, not process startup or file reads — and staged it as **`F281`** in `.ngrace/scratch/staged-findings.md` (`[verified]`, measured 2026-09-17 at `2434fd4`). This spec's six Goals are derived from that table and pay `F281` and `F282`: **(1) fewer passes** — collapse the duplicated suite invocations in `validate:ci` and the workflows; **(2) collect once, view many** — memoize the immutable predecessor-map derivation (`src/gates/ledger.ts:1134`) that `readAmendmentInstrument` (`:1187`) rebuilds once per change, 117 times per read; **(3) a selective developer-loop runner** that never gates; **(4) per-test metrics kept current**; **(5) in-process calls** for the bulk of the 163 `bun ./scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts` spawns whose contract is not the process boundary; **(6) the verification-frequency rule** — teach in `ngrace-spec`, `ngrace-plan` and `ngrace-execute` that the full CI-equivalent verification is **close-time only** — it runs at the close-time gates that prove CI-readiness, never as a per-task command. The order-of-magnitude direction is in **how often** the full verification runs, not in the suite becoming ten times faster: measured, one memo takes the suite ~1.3× and the remaining Goals approach ~2×, while a single turn currently pays the full verification six times over. The measured payload is stated as a goal, not a criterion; the criteria are relations. This spec is written at `status="draft"` and stops there: the approval write, the gates, the applied close and the flush are the authority's.
C-TEST-TIME-BUDGET-3-7950A760.Problem:
**The maintainer's complaint, in his framing.** Development is too slow and the suite is the reason. The standing ruling is **B — measured speedups, not a rewrite in another language**; it is now sharpened to an order-of-magnitude target. The four directions he named: (1) find the slowest tests; (2) reduce the number of passes; (3) collect the metrics once and take different views; (4) stop running the whole suite during fixes, run the affected tests and the whole suite once at the end, keeping per-test metrics current.
**The population — measured, not sampled.** 2026-09-17 at `2434fd4`, `bun 1.4.2`, macOS arm64. One `bun test --timeout=0 --reporter=junit --reporter-outfile=…` over the tree: `Ran 2017 tests across 64 files. [138.83s]`, exit 0. Testcase time sums to 138.62 s; **22 tests ≥ 1.0 s are 72.92 s (52.6 %)**; 41 ≥ 0.5 s are 86.76 s; 1701 < 0.05 s are 4.38 s. Per-file totals, top seven: `scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts` 42.14 s / 163 tests; `src/review/core.test.ts` 23.76 s / 188; `src/grace-context.test.ts` 19.59 s / 30; `src/gates/core.test.ts` 14.67 s / 111; `src/grace-status.test.ts` 13.41 s / 55; `src/grace-query.test.ts` 5.93 s / 42; `src/grace-lint.test.ts` 4.32 s / 114 — 123.82 s of 138.62 s (89.3 %). The slowest single tests: `src/grace-status.test.ts:1131` 11.21 s (live-repo `collectProjectStatus`), `src/review/core.test.ts:2456` 10.76 s and `:1982` 10.57 s (archive loops over every `C-*` directory), `src/grace-context.test.ts:522` 9.03 s, `scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts:1939` 3.80 s.
**The passes.** `package.json:79` chains `bun run typecheck && bun run test && … && bun run validate:cli && … && bun run validate:determinism && …`. `test` (`:67`) is the full 64-file/2017-test suite; `validate:cli` (`:69`) re-runs `src/grace-lint.test.ts src/grace-status.test.ts src/grace-query.test.ts` — 211 tests, 25.02 s, every one already executed by `test`; `validate:determinism` (`:71`) re-runs `src/review/core.test.ts src/review/scorer.test.ts` — 196 tests, 24.36 s, every one already executed by `test`. So one `bun run validate:ci` costs **2424 test runs for 2017 distinct tests**: 407 duplicate executions, 49.38 s. `.github/workflows/validate.yml:30` then runs `bun run validate:determinism` again (196 more executions, 24.36 s) after `validate:ci` already ran it. `publish.yml`'s `verify` job runs `bun run test` and then `bun run validate:cli` (another 211 duplicates on a tag push). Full-suite test wall of `validate:ci` is 138.83 + 25.02 + 24.36 = **188.21 s**, of which 49.38 s (26 %) repeats work completed moments earlier.
**The frequency — the other half of the pain, and it is teaching.** One close of the immediately preceding bundle, `C-CLONE-FAITHFUL-TESTS-1-D68520A2` (archived), ran the full suite or its CI equivalent **six times** (parsed 2026-09-17 at `2434fd4` from that bundle's `plan.xml` and `spec.xml`): T-001 `Verification` `bun run test`; T-002 `Verification` `bun run validate:ci`; the `TargetAssertions` `MustPassCommand` `bun run validate:ci` evaluated at `--assertions target`; the same evaluated again at `--assertions final`; the `AC-*` `CloseEvidence` `bun run test`; and the authority's close `validate:ci`. It also ran `bun run typecheck` ×3, `bun test scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts` ×3 and `bun test scripts/audit-regressions.test.ts` ×2. At ~140 s that is ~17 minutes of suite time in one bundle. No skill passage limits this: a search of `skills/ngrace/*/SKILL.md` for `full suite`, `whole suite`, `exactly once`, `only once`, `once per` and `per-task` finds no frequency cap — `ngrace-plan` `must_do` row 12 requires only non-empty per-task verification, and `ngrace-execute` rule 7 runs `--assertions final --run-commands`. Speed work alone leaves six runs; the frequency change alone leaves a slow suite; both together are the maintainer's ask.
**Where the wall clock goes.** Not process startup, not file reads: `bun ./src/grace.ts --version` starts in **0.09 s**; reading every archived `spec.xml`/`plan.xml` twice (11.07 MB across 117 bundles) is **7.6 ms**; reading all seven record XML files twice (1.13 MB) is **0.7 ms**. The cost is CPU **re-derivation of the same immutable corpus**. `collectProjectStatus` (`src/grace-status.ts:373`) is **11.73 s** on this tree; `collectChangeBundleStatuses` (`:165`) calls `readAmendmentInstrument(root, changeId)` (`:228`) once per bundle, and `readAmendmentInstrument` (`src/gates/ledger.ts:1187`) calls `buildPredecessorMap(projectRoot)` (`:1134`), which reads every bundle via `listChangeBundleDirs`/`replacementIdsForBundle` (`:1119`/`:1113`). Measured: `readAmendmentInstrument` ×1 = **115.4 ms**, ×117 = **9.94 s** — 117 rebuilds of one map. `src/review/core.ts:1717` calls the same function inside every `runReview` with `processAudits` on: `runReview(repoRoot, {changeId, changedFiles: [], patterns: false, joinEngine: false})` is **114.6 ms** per call and **0.0 ms** with `processAudits: false`; the archive loops at `src/review/core.test.ts:1995` and `:2483` each call it 117 times — **10.33 s per test**, twice. Separately, `scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts:50` spawns `bun ./scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts` for 163 tests; that file is 42.14 s, ~258 ms per spawn, against a validator whose entry `main(argv, cwd): number` is already exported (`:1967`).
**The three defects this names.** (a) **Duplicated passes**: 603 test executions per CI run repeat work the full suite completed. (b) **O(n²) corpus re-derivation**: the same immutable map is rebuilt once per change; the archive is read 117×117 times per top-level read. (c) **A process boundary where none is needed**: 163 validator spawns for tests whose contract is stdout and a return code, not an OS process.
**What is explicitly not to be bought.** Speed is never bought by deleting or weakening coverage. The test population does not fall and no assertion is loosened except where duplication is *proven* — the only removals proposed are the three named re-run invocations, whose test bodies and assertions stay in the suite.
**The lineage — why this is a successor, twice over.** This bundle supersedes `C-TEST-TIME-BUDGET-2-3EC1F016`, whose **deliverable was carried to completion and stands green** — committed at `68ec888` (suite 138.83 s → 73.01 s; the memo, the selective runner, per-test metrics, the in-process validator conversion and the `close-time only` rule all landed), and nothing about the code is in question. The supersede is **a governance defect, not a code defect**, and the authority staged it as **`F285`**. That bundle's approved spec assigns the payment to the authority — "the approval write, the gates, the applied close and the flush are the authority's" — and excludes the record from `AC-NO-OTHER-SRC`, but its approved plan's `ObservedWriteScope` named **25 files and no record file**, because the bundle carried no payment task. The authority's `--flush` therefore wrote `findings.xml`, `decisions.xml` and `registry.xml` outside the declared scope, and `ngrace review` returned **three `review.scope-outside-write-scope` errors**, one per record file. **No ordering avoids it**: the flush refuses once the bundle is archived (`flush-row-not-active` checks `.ngrace/changes/active/<change>`), and `--retire` needs the row to exist before it can move it, so the flush must run while the bundle is active — exactly the window the scope audit watches. Only a declaration in the plan could have prevented it, and the remedy is the successor's **plan**, not this spec: the spec already authorises the record writes. This successor carries the predecessor's bytes; beyond the id, this paragraph, the reset `status` and dropped `Replacement`, and the base line's stale buffer enumeration, no Goal, Constraint, NonGoal, criterion or Assumption is touched.
**The lineage of the narrowing, which stands.** The first supersede remains the reason Goal 1(a) is `validate:ci`-only. The approved `C-TEST-TIME-BUDGET-1-98736D59` (ratified, gated, archived `superseded`) confined its write scope for the duplicate-pass remedy to `validate:ci` and the workflows, **but drafted Goal 1(a) as removing `bun run validate:cli` from `validate:ci` and `validate:release`**. Two shipped guards require `validate:release` to invoke `validate:cli` (`scripts/validate-marketplace.ts:336`–`338`, `scripts/release-checklist.ts:250`), and `bun run validate:marketplace` is itself a member of `validate:ci` — so the dedup reddened CI, and neither guard file was in the approved write scope or in `AC-NO-OTHER-SRC`'s excludes. Driven at plan time on a `b9b45f3` copy: `bun run ./scripts/validate-marketplace.ts` exit 1, `package.json: validate:release must invoke validate:cli`; the release checklist reported the same. That bundle was uncloseable as approved. The authority ruled **narrow, do not widen** and superseded it, staging **`F282`**. `validate:release` keeps its `validate:cli` and is untouched — it runs at release time, not inside a development turn, so narrowing to `validate:ci` keeps the entire measured saving, leaves both guards green, and forces no new file into scope; no guard constrains `validate:ci`'s composition (`scripts/release-checklist.ts:245` asserts only that the script exists).
**The base.** Branch `c-test-time-budget` at **`2434fd467458e15c12414a74e37b09f9d71bdfd2`** (= merged `main`), tree clean, `.ngrace/changes/active/` holding `.gitkeep` only, 117 archive directories. The buffer holds `F270`, `F280`, `F281`, `F282`, `F283`, `F284` and `F285`; the record's max finding is `F279` (retired); the executor staged `F281` and the authority `F282`, and this bundle pays **`F281`** and **`F282`**.

Goals.Goal: **(1) Fewer passes — one suite run per CI run.** The duplicated suite invocations are removed and nothing else: (a) `bun run validate:cli` leaves `validate:ci` (`package.json:79`) — its 211 tests are already executed by `bun run test` in the same script. `validate:release` keeps its `validate:cli` and is untouched by this bundle: it runs at release time, never inside a development turn, and two shipped guards assert that composition (`scripts/validate-marketplace.ts:336`–`338`, `scripts/release-checklist.ts:250`). (b) `validate:determinism` (`package.json:71`) loses its `bun test --timeout=0 src/review/core.test.ts src/review/scorer.test.ts` prefix (196 tests already executed by `bun run test`) and keeps `bun run ./scripts/validate-determinism.ts`, which itself performs the two-run identity and the D4 ratchet; (c) the duplicate standalone `Run determinism and corpus ratchet gate (D4)` step (`.github/workflows/validate.yml:30`) is removed because `validate:ci` already runs that member; (d) `publish.yml`'s `verify` job loses its `CLI validation` step (`bun run validate:cli`) because `bun run test` in the same job already executes those 211 tests. `validate:cli` remains a runnable standalone command (the Windows job's `bun run test <files>` + `validate:cli` pair runs **disjoint** file sets and is not duplication, so it is untouched). A guard in `scripts/audit-regressions.test.ts` asserts the relation structurally: an aggregate script that invokes the full suite invokes no other `bun test`, and a workflow job that runs `validate:ci` or the full suite runs no second suite command. `scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts`'s and `scripts/publish-workflow.test.ts`'s composition assertions are updated to the deduped shape (their positive coverage is preserved, not deleted).

**(2) Collect once, view many — memoize the immutable predecessor map.** `buildPredecessorMap` (`src/gates/ledger.ts:1134`) is derived from immutable on-disk bundle metadata; it is computed at most once per **resolved project root** per process, validated by a cheap revision token recomputed on every call — the sorted `(bundle name, spec/plan size, mtimeMs)` for the active and archive bundle directories — so an added, removed, renamed or in-place-edited bundle invalidates the entry. The cached value is returned as a frozen, read-only view (`chainDepth` already only reads it). No caller-visible behaviour changes: `readAmendmentInstrument`, `collectProjectStatus` and `runReview` return byte-identical results for the same tree. Measured before: `collectProjectStatus(REPO_ROOT)` 11.73 s, of which `readAmendmentInstrument` ×117 is 9.94 s; `runReview(REPO_ROOT, {changeId})` ×117 is 10.33 s in each of two archive tests. The plan adds the invalidation and mutation-boundary tests to `src/gates/core.test.ts`; the target is a Goal with a measured after, not a pinned figure. No other parse is memoized unless the plan's own measurement shows it pays.

**(3) A selective developer-loop runner that never gates.** `scripts/test-affected.ts` (new), run as `bun run test:affected` (`package.json`), takes a base ref (default `origin/main`, overridable), reads the changed files from git, maps each to the test files that exercise it (path convention plus an explicit dependency table in the script), prints the selection and the reason for each, and runs only those with `bun test --timeout=0 …`. It is **fail-safe**: an unmapped changed source file under `src/` or `scripts/`, an empty or unavailable diff, or a merge-base failure selects the **full suite** rather than fewer tests. `scripts/test-affected.test.ts` (new) proves the selection on a synthetic diff and proves the fail-safe fallback. The hard rule: **a selective run never gates.** `validate:ci` and `validate:release` keep the full `bun run test`; no `CloseEvidence` command anywhere may invoke the runner, and a guard reddens if one does.

**(4) Per-test metrics kept current.** `scripts/test-metrics.ts` (new), run as `bun run test:metrics`, executes the suite once with `--reporter=junit` and writes a committed `test-metrics.json` holding, per test file, the test count and total ms, plus every individual test's ms and file, a `schemaVersion` and the generation date — and **no hostname or machine identifier** (this repository is public). It prints the slowest tests. The suite need not run the meter; `scripts/test-metrics.test.ts` (new) asserts the freshness relation: every `*.test.ts` in the tree appears exactly once in the artifact, the artifact's per-file counts match the tree, and the artifact carries no machine identifier. The artifact records durations; **no criterion compares a duration to a threshold** — the regression signal is a regenerated diff against the committed baseline, and a planted slower test is proven to move it (a relation), not a wall-clock gate. The `test-metrics.json` read is a tracked-path read and must be committed before the fixture-read guard runs.

**(5) In-process calls where the process boundary is not the contract.** The bulk of `scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts`'s 163 `runValidator` spawns (42.14 s, ~258 ms each) are moved to an in-process helper that calls the validator's already-exported `main(argv, cwd): number` (`scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:1967`) and captures stdout/stderr through an injectable writer seam, so no process is created. The spawn is **kept** — and said so in the test — exactly where the contract under test *is* the process boundary: the exit-code discriminations and the CWD-relative behaviour. The test population does not fall; every assertion keeps its subject. A guard or an instrumented assertion states the bounded spawn count so a later re-spawn is visible.

**(6) The verification-frequency rule, taught.** The full, CI-equivalent verification is never avoided — it is what proves the branch will merge, and it runs inside the turn. The rule is about *how many times*, not *whether*: the full CI-equivalent verification is **close-time only** — it runs at `--assertions final --run-commands`, and at the close's `CloseEvidence` only where a criterion is genuinely about the whole suite. It is never a per-task command. Written into three skills, in both trees: `skills/ngrace/ngrace-plan/SKILL.md` (a new `must_do` row — a task's `Verification` names the **narrowest instrument** that exercises that task's subject, the whole suite is not a per-task command, and a `TargetAssertions` `MustPassCommand` does not duplicate what `final` runs); `skills/ngrace/ngrace-spec/SKILL.md` (`acceptance_criteria_anchors` — a `CloseEvidence` `Command` names the narrow instrument unless the criterion is genuinely about the whole suite; `AC-CLONE-FAITHFUL` is the legitimate whole-suite case and stays legitimate); and `skills/ngrace/ngrace-execute/SKILL.md` (`execution_rules` rule 7 — the full verification runs once, at `final`; per-task verification is the task's own narrowest command). Each canonical skill is mirrored byte-identically into `plugins/ngrace/skills/ngrace/*`. The load-bearing tokens (`close-time only`, `narrowest instrument`) are added to `TAUGHT_RULES` in `scripts/check-teaching-surface.ts` and to the fixture table in `scripts/check-teaching-surface.test.ts`, so a later softening reddens. This Goal does not weaken `AC-SELECTIVE-NOT-GATE`: a narrow **task** verification is a named command whose subject is the task, not a selective run, and the full verification still runs at `final` and at the close.

Constraints.Constraint: **Tier and anchor.** Ceremony tier **T3** (architectural-in-method: the change moves the taught lifecycle contract across `ngrace-spec`, `ngrace-plan` and `ngrace-execute`, both skill trees, the taught-rule token tables, the skill-footprint pins and `README.md`, and the taught rule must be designed so it does not contradict `AC-SELECTIVE-NOT-GATE` — it changes methodology, not one package). Roadmap `RM-GOVERNED-PATH`. Base commit `2434fd467458e15c12414a74e37b09f9d71bdfd2`. Two module-ownable paths this bundle writes: `src/gates/ledger.ts` (`LINKS: M-GATES`, `src/gates/ledger.ts:5`) and the three canonical `skills/ngrace/*/SKILL.md` files (`M-SKILLS`). Every other forced file is `package.json`, a workflow, a `scripts/` path, a `*.test.ts`, the packaged skill mirror, `README.md` or `test-metrics.json`, and `isModuleOwnableWritePath` (`src/lint/core.ts:734`) is false for all of them. `AffectedAreas` therefore names exactly `M-GATES` and `M-SKILLS`; the module list appears **once** (`F136.1`). The plan's `DurableScope` anchors `M-GATES` for `src/gates/ledger.ts`.

**A selective run never gates.** This is the load-bearing constraint, written after `C-CLONE-FAITHFUL-TESTS-1-D68520A2`, whose local green signed off a suite that died in every clone. The dev-loop runner is a fix convenience only. CI and the close always run the whole suite: `validate:ci` and `validate:release` keep `bun run test`; every `CloseEvidence` command in this bundle names `bun run test`, a specific `bun test --timeout=0 <file>`, `bun ./src/grace.ts lint --path . --fail-on warnings`, or a `git diff --exit-code` against a named base — **never** `test:affected`. A guard reddens if any active or archived spec or plan `CloseEvidence` invokes the runner.

**Memoize only immutable data; prove the boundary.** Caching a derivation of immutable on-disk metadata is safe; caching a mutable fixture buys order-dependent flakiness. The predecessor-map cache is keyed by the resolved project root and validated by the sorted `(bundle name, spec/plan byte size, mtimeMs)` revision of the active and archive bundle directories, recomputed on each call; a change to that revision rebuilds the map. The value handed back is a frozen copy, so a caller that mutates a returned view cannot corrupt the cache. Two directions are driven in `src/gates/core.test.ts`: (i) mutate the returned structure, call again, and observe the original unchanged; (ii) add/remove a superseding bundle in a temp root, call again, and observe the new chain depth. A writer that edits a bundle in place without changing size or mtime must invalidate explicitly; no shipped writer does so (the supersede path moves or restamps the bundle).

**Speed is never bought with coverage.** The executed test population does not fall relative to base `2434fd467458e15c12414a74e37b09f9d71bdfd2`, and no assertion is loosened. The only removed work is the three **proven duplicates**: `validate:ci`'s `validate:cli` invocation (211 tests already run by `bun run test` in the same script), `validate:determinism`'s `bun test src/review/core.test.ts src/review/scorer.test.ts` prefix (196 tests already run by `bun run test`), and `validate.yml:30`'s standalone re-run of that same member (and `publish.yml`'s `validate:cli` after `bun run test`). Their test bodies stay in the suite and are not edited. A guard asserts the per-test-file test counts at HEAD are not below base.

**No per-test timeouts; the fixture-read guard ships.** `bun test --timeout=0` stays on every invocation; no numeric per-test timeout is introduced (`findTimeoutPins`); every suite-running workflow job keeps `timeout-minutes: 30` (`suiteJobsMissingCeiling`). The new `test-metrics.json` is a repository-relative tracked path; no `.ts` under `src/` or `scripts/` may pass a git-ignored or untracked path to a filesystem read (`findUntrackedFixtureReads`), so the artifact is `git add`ed as part of the change before that guard is green.

**The order of magnitude is frequency, not a ten-times-fast suite.** The corrected premise: the maintainer's order-of-magnitude direction comes from **how often** the full verification runs, not from the suite becoming ten times faster. Measured, the suite itself reaches ~1.3× on the Goal 2 memo alone and approaches ~2× with the remaining Goals; the development win is that a turn pays the full verification **once** instead of six times. No criterion in this spec pins a ten-times figure; the criteria are the relations (once per CI run, once per turn, byte-identical derivation results).

AcceptanceCriteria.AC-FEWER-PASSES:
Within one `bun run validate:ci`, each discovered test file is executed exactly once: the aggregate script `validate:ci` contains the full suite (`bun run test`) and no other `bun test` invocation, and no workflow job that runs `validate:ci` or the full suite runs a second suite command. The guard in `scripts/audit-regressions.test.ts` parses `package.json` and both workflow files and reddens on a re-introduced subset re-run; driven both ways (clean tree green, planted re-run red).
bun test --timeout=0 scripts/audit-regressions.test.ts bun run test
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-COLLECT-ONCE:
`buildPredecessorMap` is computed at most once per resolved project root per process while the bundle revision token is unchanged, for both `collectProjectStatus(REPO_ROOT)` and `runReview(REPO_ROOT, {changeId, changedFiles: [], patterns: false, joinEngine: false})`; the results are byte-identical to the unmemoized derivation for the same tree. A second call over an unchanged tree performs no bundle XML parse; a changed revision token rebuilds. The relation is evaluated by `src/gates/core.test.ts`, not by a wall-clock figure.
bun test --timeout=0 src/gates/core.test.ts bun test --timeout=0 src/grace-status.test.ts
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-MEMO-BOUNDARY:
Mutation of a returned view does not affect another caller, and tree mutation is observed: (i) mutate the structure the API returns, call again, and the value is unchanged; (ii) add or remove a superseding bundle in a temp root, call again, and the chain depth reflects it. Driven both directions in `src/gates/core.test.ts`; a planted mutation that leaves a stale cache reddens the criterion.
bun test --timeout=0 src/gates/core.test.ts
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-SELECTIVE-NOT-GATE:
`scripts/test-affected.ts` exists and, on a synthetic diff touching one source file, selects that file's test and not the whole suite; on an unmapped source change or an unavailable diff it selects the full suite. `validate:ci` and `validate:release` contain `bun run test` and do not contain the runner; no `CloseEvidence` in any active or archived spec or plan contains the runner token, and a guard reddens if one does. The runner is never a `CloseEvidence` command of this bundle.
bun test --timeout=0 scripts/test-affected.test.ts
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-METRICS-FRESH:
`test-metrics.json` lists every `*.test.ts` under the tree exactly once with its test count and total ms, and the artifact's counts agree with the tree; adding or removing a test file without regenerating reddens the freshness guard; a planted slower test is driven to appear in the emitted ranking (a relation, not a threshold). The artifact carries no hostname or machine identifier.
bun test --timeout=0 scripts/test-metrics.test.ts
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-INPROCESS:
The bulk of `scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts` drives the validator through its exported `main(argv, cwd)` in-process, and the `spawnSync("bun", [SCRIPT, …])` executions are bounded to the tests whose contract is the process exit code or the CWD boundary; every assertion keeps its subject and the file's test count does not fall. The in-process path is discriminated (a planted violation returns non-zero) and at least one exit-code/CWD contract is still driven through a real spawn.
bun test --timeout=0 scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-VERIFICATION-FREQUENCY:
The three skills teach the frequency rule in both trees, byte-identically: `ngrace-plan`'s `must_do` carries the token `narrowest instrument`; `ngrace-spec`'s `acceptance_criteria_anchors` and `ngrace-execute`'s `execution_rules` carry the token `close-time only`; `TAUGHT_RULES` in `scripts/check-teaching-surface.ts` and the fixture table in `scripts/check-teaching-surface.test.ts` carry the same tokens; the canonical and packaged skill bodies are byte-identical. The rule does not weaken `AC-SELECTIVE-NOT-GATE`: the full CI-equivalent suite still runs at `final` and at the close, and no `CloseEvidence` names the runner.
bun run validate:teaching-surface bun test --timeout=0 scripts/skill-contracts.test.ts
